name: factory-industrial-a
prompt:
Use case: redesign / style-transfer. Create ONE polished industrial workshop game-level concept by editing reference IMAGE 1. Preserve its wide high-oblique camera, full rectangular hall perimeter, low cream rear wall with blue clerestory windows, hall proportions, six production bays in the upper half, long horizontal conveyor across the middle, loading truck at right. The whole floor must remain visible from overhead, no roof. IMAGE 2 is just a detail of the upper line. IMAGE 3 is only a palette and painterly rendering reference, NOT a toy-form reference.
OWNER CORRECTION: this is a REAL MECHANICAL FACTORY for a curious child, NOT a toy factory, nursery, playroom, teddy-bear warehouse or miniature plastic playset. Build credible functional steel machinery with cast frames, bolts, rivets, realistic gear teeth, separate motors, shafts, belt pulleys, chains, steel guide rails and hydraulic pistons. Clear cheerful daylight, warm cream architecture, brushed gray steel, yellow-black safety edges, teal and restrained coral machine panels. Clean, well maintained, not grimy or dark; soft hand-painted finish compatible with the reference map, but materials and proportions feel engineered.
ALL FOUR GAMEPLAY IDEAS MUST BE VISUALLY DISTINCT: (1) a waist-high electrical control cabinet with its door open, clearly showing exactly four large square rotatable puzzle tiles in a 2x2 grid with thick simple cable or pipe path segments; (2) a horizontal rail trolley with a large forward/back lever and a separate vertical lift with an up/down lever; (3) an exposed gear train with three clearly different gear diameters, attached motor and a big analog speed dial with needle; (4) a sturdy two-post industrial press with TWO widely separated big palm buttons on its front control bar. Add a small connector bench with round, square and triangular cable plugs and matching sockets; bold pictograms rather than tiny labels. Pipework with large hand-wheel valves, overhead beam hoist, safe low railings around active stations, broad walkways. Avoid people near moving gears. Stations must be large enough to read at tablet scale and not crowded.
Use the lower half for additional mechanics: rail trolley, vertical lift, orderly raw material racks with steel rods/coils, and a gear demonstration station. Keep the six upper stations and central conveyor spatially recognizable. Wide clear navigation lane along the conveyor, separated work islands, controls facing the camera. No UI, title, labels, words, numbers, watermarks or cutaway inset panels. Landscape composition around 1600x1100, same hall framing as IMAGE 1. Single coherent scene, not a collage.
VARIANT A — CLASSIC MACHINE SHOP. Main floor is warm light gray concrete with broad cream pedestrian routes. Teal cast-iron machine bases, large steel flywheels and coral motors. Lower-left: a short straight horizontal double-rail trolley carrying a steel block, large reverse lever at its near end. Lower center: three-diameter open gear train mounted on a low rigid steel frame with dial and motor, plus connector bench. Lower-right: compact yellow beam hoist over a clear vertical lift cage, adjacent orderly steel stock rack. Upper line includes the open 2x2 cabinet, lathe-like motor/shaft station and two-hand press. Prioritize strong mechanical silhouettes and generous space; all mechanics equally readable.
